@@ -0,0 +1,175 @@
+"""cycle-129 FR-7 (SDD D-7.3; sprint-257 Task 3.2, AC-3.2) — thinking traces from local
+reasoning models on the OpenAI paths.
+
+* Streamed `delta.reasoning_content` deltas count as progress for the recovery tracker
+  (they satisfy the first-token deadline) and never reach `content`; they land in
+  `thinking`.
+* Leading `<think>…</think>` blocks and an unterminated leading `<think>` are stripped
+  from the content before qualification on the streaming and the non-streaming path;
+  `thinking_stripped` is recorded in the result metadata (cheval copies it to MODELINV).
+* The model's `streaming_recovery` block reaches the stream parser.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import sys
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any, Dict, Iterator, List
+
+import pytest
+
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]))
+
+from loa_cheval.providers import openai_adapter as oa  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.providers.openai_adapter import OpenAIAdapter  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.providers.openai_streaming import parse_openai_chat_stream, strip_thinking_blocks  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.streaming import StreamingRecoveryAbort  # noqa: E402
+from loa_cheval.types import CompletionRequest, ModelConfig, ProviderConfig  # noqa: E402
+
+
+def _sse(*payloads: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[bytes]:
+    return [f"data: {json.dumps(p)}\n\n".encode() for p in payloads] + [b"data: [DONE]\n\n"]
+
+
+def _delta(**delta: Any) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    return {"choices": [{"delta": delta, "finish_reason": None}], "model": "m"}
+
+
+class _Clock:
+    """Advances `step` seconds on every read — each SSE event costs `step` seconds."""
+
+    def __init__(self, step: float):
+        self.t = 0.0
+        self.step = step
+
+    def __call__(self) -> float:
+        self.t += self.step
+        return self.t
+
+
+SLOW = {"streaming_recovery": {"first_token_deadline_s": 5}}
+
+
+def test_reasoning_deltas_keep_the_tracker_alive_and_never_reach_content():
+    chunks = _sse(
+        _delta(reasoning_content="Let me look at the diff. "),
+        _delta(reasoning_content="The loop is off by one. "),
+        _delta(reasoning_content="So the finding is the bound."),
+        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
+        {"choices": [{"delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}], "model": "m"},
+    )
+    # every event costs 3 s against a 5 s first-token deadline: content arrives at ~15 s
+    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))
+    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
+    assert "off by one" in (result.thinking or "")
+    assert "Let me look" not in result.content
+    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True
+    assert result.metadata["streaming_recovery"]["config_applied"]["first_token_deadline_s"] == 5.0
+
+
+def test_control_without_reasoning_progress_the_deadline_fires():
+    chunks = _sse(
+        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},     # keep-alive-shaped frames: no content, no reasoning
+        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
+        {"choices": [], "model": "m"},
+        _delta(content='{"findings": []}'),
+    )
+    with pytest.raises(StreamingRecoveryAbort) as info:
+        parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", model_data=SLOW, now_provider=_Clock(3.0))
+    assert info.value.reason == "first_token_deadline"
+
+
+def test_reasoning_alias_key_and_no_empty_content_abort():
+    # 300 reasoning deltas exceed the 200-token empty-content window if they were fed as content
+    many = [_delta(reasoning="step ") for _ in range(300)]
+    chunks = _sse(*many, _delta(content="answer"))
+    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", now_provider=_Clock(0.001))
+    assert result.content == "answer"
+    assert result.thinking.startswith("step step")
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("raw, content, removed, stripped", [
+    ("<think>plan</think>\n{\"a\": 1}", '{"a": 1}', "plan", True),
+    ("  <THINK>one</THINK><think>two</think> answer", "answer", "one\ntwo", True),
+    ("<think>never closed, the budget ran out", "", "never closed, the budget ran out", True),
+    ('{"note": "the template uses <think> tags"}', '{"note": "the template uses <think> tags"}', "", False),
+    ("answer first <think>late</think>", "answer first <think>late</think>", "", False),
+    ("", "", "", False),
+], ids=["block", "two-blocks-case", "unterminated", "inside-answer-kept", "not-leading-kept", "empty"])
+def test_strip_thinking_blocks(raw, content, removed, stripped):
+    assert strip_thinking_blocks(raw) == (content, removed, stripped)
+
+
+def test_think_block_stripped_on_the_streaming_path():
+    chunks = _sse(_delta(content="<think>reasoning "), _delta(content="here</think>\n"),
+                  _delta(content='{"findings": [1]}'))
+    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="local", now_provider=_Clock(0.01))
+    assert result.content == '{"findings": [1]}'
+    assert result.thinking == "reasoning here"
+    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True
+
+
+def test_hosted_shaped_stream_records_thinking_stripped_false():
+    chunks = _sse(_delta(content='{"findings": []}'))
+    result = parse_openai_chat_stream(iter(chunks), provider="openai", now_provider=_Clock(0.01))
+    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
+    assert result.thinking is None
+    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is False
+
+
+# --- through the adapter -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+
+def _adapter(**model_kwargs: Any) -> OpenAIAdapter:
+    return OpenAIAdapter(ProviderConfig(
+        name="local", type="openai_compat", endpoint="http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1", auth="", keyless=True,
+        allow_insecure_endpoint="127.0.0.1",
+        models={"m": ModelConfig(capabilities=["chat"], context_window=32768, endpoint_family="chat",
+                                 dispatch_group="local", **model_kwargs)},
+    ))
+
+
+def _req() -> CompletionRequest:
+    return CompletionRequest(messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "review"}], model="m", max_tokens=64)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("message, thinking", [
+    ({"content": "<think>weighing it</think>{\"findings\": []}"}, "weighing it"),
+    ({"content": "{\"findings\": []}", "reasoning_content": "weighing it"}, "weighing it"),
+], ids=["inline-think", "reasoning_content"])
+def test_non_streaming_path_strips_and_records(monkeypatch, message, thinking):
+    monkeypatch.setenv("LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING", "1")
+    monkeypatch.setattr(oa, "http_post", lambda *a, **k: (200, {"choices": [{"message": message}], "model": "m",
+                                                               "usage": {"prompt_tokens": 1, "completion_tokens": 1}}))
+    result = _adapter().complete(_req())
+    assert result.content == '{"findings": []}'
+    assert result.thinking == thinking
+    assert result.metadata["thinking_stripped"] is True
+
+
+def test_adapter_passes_the_models_streaming_recovery_block(monkeypatch):
+    monkeypatch.delenv("LOA_CHEVAL_DISABLE_STREAMING", raising=False)
+    seen: Dict[str, Any] = {}
+    real = oa.parse_openai_chat_stream
+

+  if [[ ! "$n" =~ ^[0-9]{1,2}$ ]]; then log "WARN: ${label} could not be read or has over 99 entries — ignored"; return 0; fi
+  (( n == 0 )) && return 0
+  rows=$(yq -o=json -I=0 eval ".flatline_protocol.${config_key}.advisory_voices[] | [tag, .]" "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
+    | jq -rn '[inputs] | to_entries[]
+        | (.value[0] | if type == "string" and test("\\A[!A-Za-z0-9._/:-]{1,64}\\z") then . else "unreadable" end) as $tg
+        | if $tg == "!!str" and (.value[1] | type) == "string" and (.value[1] | test("\\A[A-Za-z0-9._/:-]{1,128}\\z"))

+# --- locality (D-8.1): one classification per hop, from lib/hop-locality.py over the merged catalog + project config ----
+_ADV_LOC_TSV=""       # "<hop>\t<provider>\t<local|hosted>\t<reason>" lines, this process
+_ADV_LOC_REFUSED=""   # "<role>\t<hop>\t<provider>" lines — every hosted hop refused at plan time (the envelope names them)
+_ADV_LOC_KEPT=""      # _adv_locality_filter's answer (a global: the caller runs it at top level, never in $(...))
+_adv_locality_row() { awk -F'\t' -v h="$1" '$1 == h { print; exit }' <<<"$_ADV_LOC_TSV"; }
+_adv_locality_load() {  # <hop>... — classify the hops this process has not classified yet (one python call); fail closed
+  local -a new=(); local h line rows="" cat="${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}"
+  for h in "$@"; do [[ -n "$h" && -z "$(_adv_locality_row "$h")" ]] && new+=("$h"); done
+  (( ${#new[@]} > 0 )) || return 0
+  rows=$(python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$cat" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" -- "${new[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  for h in "${new[@]}"; do
+    line=$(awk -F'\t' -v h="$h" '$1 == h && NF >= 4 { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    [[ -n "$line" ]] || line="${h}"$'\t'"unknown"$'\t'"hosted"$'\t'"classifier_unavailable"   # (no answer is a hosted hop)
+    _ADV_LOC_TSV+="${line}"$'\n'
+  done
+}
+_adv_hop_is_local() { _adv_locality_load "$1"; [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$1" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; }
+_adv_locality_filter() {  # <role> <hop>... → _ADV_LOC_KEPT: the local hops in order; each hosted one is refused by name, once per role
+  local role="$1" h p; shift
+  _ADV_LOC_KEPT=""
+  _adv_locality_load "$@"
+  for h in "$@"; do
+    [[ -n "$h" ]] || continue
+    if [[ "$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f3)" == "local" ]]; then _ADV_LOC_KEPT+="${_ADV_LOC_KEPT:+ }$h"; continue; fi
+    p=$(_adv_locality_row "$h" | cut -f2); p="${p:-unknown}"
+    if ! grep -qxF "${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}" <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"; then
+      _ADV_LOC_REFUSED+="${role}"$'\t'"${h}"$'\t'"${p}"$'\n'
+      log "locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop $h ($p)"
+    fi
+  done
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_locality_refused_json() {  # → [{role, alias, provider}] for the envelope
+  printf '%s' "$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED" | jq -R -s 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0) | split("\t") | {role: .[0], alias: .[1], provider: .[2]})'
+}
+# The one sentence the config comment and the audit output carry (D-8.1).
+_ADV_LOC_DEGRADED_SENTENCE="locality: local_voices — with one local family the companion is not an independent second voice (duplicate_voice, or not planned), so every security audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; adversarial-review-gate.sh and verdict-derive.sh treat this envelope exactly as they treat any other."
+
+# --- the budget gate (D-7.4, D-7.6): every planned voice at its catalog price ------------------------------------------
+_ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL=0
+_ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="[]"
+_adv_budget_estimate() {  # <estimated input tokens> <role>=<hop>... → _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL (cents) and _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES (JSON);
+  # each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 output tokens × output rate (micro-USD per Mtok → cents: ÷ 10^10, each term
+  # truncated, as the fixed-rate formula was). An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok and is said;
+  # a zero-priced one estimates 0 and is said too.
+  local tokens="$1"; shift
+  local -a roles=() hops=() args=()
+  local rv rows="" line c_in c_out total=0 voices="[]"
+  for rv in "$@"; do roles+=("${rv%%=*}"); hops+=("${rv#*=}"); args+=(--alias "${rv#*=}"); done
+  if (( ${#hops[@]} > 0 )); then
+    rows=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing \
+      --catalog "${LOA_MODEL_CONFIG:-$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml}" --config "${CONFIG_FILE:-}" "${args[@]}" 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+  fi
+  local k _bv_role _bv_hop _bv_src _bv_in _bv_out _bv_cents
+  for (( k = 0; k < ${#hops[@]}; k++ )); do
+    _bv_role="${roles[$k]}"; _bv_hop="${hops[$k]}"   # (a role word and a validated hop name — the jq operands below are small)
+    line=$(awk -v a="alias=$_bv_hop" '$1 == a { print; exit }' <<<"$rows")
+    _bv_in=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_out=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9][0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    _bv_src=$(sed -n 's/.* pricing_source=\([a-z_]*\)$/\1/p' <<<"$line")
+    if [[ ! "$_bv_in" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || ! "$_bv_out" =~ ^[0-9]{1,12}$ || "$_bv_src" == "unknown" || -z "$_bv_src" ]]; then
+      _bv_in=10000000; _bv_out=30000000; _bv_src="fallback"
+      log "budget: no catalog price for $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice"
+    elif (( _bv_in == 0 && _bv_out == 0 )); then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c"
+    elif [[ "$_bv_src" == "stale_catalog" ]]; then
+      log "budget: $_bv_hop ($_bv_role) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given"
+    fi
+    c_in=$(( tokens * _bv_in / 10000000000 )); c_out=$(( 2000 * _bv_out / 10000000000 )); _bv_cents=$(( c_in + c_out ))
+    total=$(( total + _bv_cents ))
+    voices=$(jq -c --arg r "$_bv_role" --arg h "$_bv_hop" --arg s "$_bv_src" --argjson c "$_bv_cents" --argjson i "$_bv_in" --argjson o "$_bv_out" \
+      '. + [{role: $r, alias: $h, estimated_cents: $c, input_per_mtok: $i, output_per_mtok: $o, pricing_source: $s}]' <<<"$voices")
+  done
+  _ADV_BUDGET_TOTAL="$total"; _ADV_BUDGET_VOICES="$voices"
+  log "budget: estimate ${total}c over ${#hops[@]} planned voice(s) ($(jq -r 'map("\(.role) \(.alias) \(.estimated_cents)c") | join(", ")' <<<"$voices"))"
+}
+
+# --- advisory voices (D-7.4): after the counted voices, concurrently, one wall clock, findings only under advisory_voices[] ---
+_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""   # "pid=token" pairs of the live advisory walkers (the reapers kill only the process forked)
+_adv_reap_advisory() {
+  local e p
+  for e in ${_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS:-}; do
+    p="${e%%=*}"
+    [[ "$p" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
+    _adv_is_same "$p" "$e" && { _adv_kill_tree "$p" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true; }
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_walk() {  # <voice dir> <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias> — one advisory voice: the hop, then
+  # process_findings (the same schema, qualification and KF-004 repair rules as a counted voice); its rejected payloads never
+  # land beside the envelope (verdict-derive counts those), and the result is published whole
+  local d="$1" type="$2" sprint_id="$3" timeout="$4" diff_files="$5" alias="$6" raw="" rc=0 res="" st=""
+  export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REJECT_SIDECAR_DISABLE=1
+  export _ADV_SIDECAR_TAG="advisory"
+  raw=$(_adv_invoke_hop "$alias" "$d/system-prompt.txt" "$d/user-prompt.txt" "$alias" "$timeout" "$d/vq-advisory.json" "$type" "$SCRIPT_DIR/../schemas/wire/dissent-${type}.wire.json") || rc=$?
+  printf '%s' "$rc" > "$d/rc"
+  res=$(process_findings "$raw" "$type" "$alias" "$sprint_id" "$rc" "$diff_files") || res=""
+  if [[ -n "$res" ]]; then st=$(_extract_result_status "$res") || st=""; fi
+  [[ -n "$st" ]] || st="malformed_response"
+  printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/result.json.tmp" && mv -f "$d/result.json.tmp" "$d/result.json"
+  printf '%s' "$st" > "$d/status"
+}
+_adv_run_advisory_voices() {  # <type> <sprint id> <timeout> <diff files> <alias>... — every voice started at once under
+  # $CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT seconds of wall clock for all of them; a voice still running then is killed and marked timed_out.
+  # Each voice's files are under $_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory/<n>/
+  local type="$1" sprint_id="$2" timeout="$3" diff_files="$4"; shift 4
+  local root="$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/advisory" n=0 a d pid tok e deadline alive
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  for a in "$@"; do
+    n=$((n + 1)); d="$root/$n"
+    mkdir -p "$d" 2>/dev/null || continue
+    printf '%s' "$a" > "$d/alias"
+    if cp -f "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/system-prompt.txt" "$_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR/user-prompt.txt" "$d/" 2>/dev/null; then
+      ( _adv_advisory_walk "$d" "$type" "$sprint_id" "$timeout" "$diff_files" "$a" ) >"$d/log" 2>&1 &
+      pid=$!
+      tok=$(_adv_fork_token "$pid") || tok=""
+      _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS+="${pid}=$(_adv_tok_word "$tok") "
+      printf '%s' "$pid" > "$d/pid"
+    else
+      printf 'prompt_copy_failed' > "$d/status"
+    fi
+  done
+  deadline=$(( $(date +%s) + CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT ))
+  while :; do
+    alive=0
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do _adv_is_same "${e%%=*}" "$e" && { alive=1; break; }; done
+    (( alive )) || break
+    (( $(date +%s) < deadline )) || break
+    sleep 0.2
+  done
+  for (( a = 1; a <= n; a++ )); do
+    d="$root/$a"; [[ -s "$d/pid" ]] || continue
+    pid=$(cat "$d/pid" 2>/dev/null || true)
+    for e in $_ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS; do
+      [[ "${e%%=*}" == "$pid" ]] || continue
+      if _adv_is_same "$pid" "$e"; then
+        : > "$d/timed_out"
+        _adv_kill_tree "$pid" KILL >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
+        log "Advisory voice $(cat "$d/alias"): still running at the ${CONF_ADVISORY_TIMEOUT}s advisory wall clock — killed (timed_out)"
+      fi
+      wait "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true
+    done
+  done
+  _ADV_ADVISORY_PIDS=""
+  return 0
+}
+_adv_advisory_block() {  # <type> <counted result json file> <diff file> <alias>…(planned, in order) — the advisory_voices[]
+  # array on stdout: each planned voice's findings (hallucination-filtered, tagged voice: advisory, linked by duplicate_of to a
+  # counted finding with the same file, overlapping lines and the same category) in config order, then every alias locality refused
+  local type="$1" counted="$2" diff_file="$3"; shift 3
+  # (every jq operand below is a small reviewed scalar — a validated alias, a status word, an error cut to 200 characters, a
+  # whole number; the envelopes travel as files)
+  local root="${_ADVERSARIAL_WORKDIR:-}/advisory" _av_n=0 _av_alias d st res entry _av_rc _av_err
+  mkdir -p "$root" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+  local blk="$root/entries.jsonl"; : > "$blk" || return 1
+  for _av_alias in "$@"; do
+    _av_n=$((_av_n + 1)); d="$root/$_av_n"; st=""; res='{}'; _av_err=""
+    if [[ -e "$d/timed_out" ]]; then st="timed_out"
+    elif [[ -s "$d/result.json" ]] && jq -e 'type == "object"' "$d/result.json" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      res=$(cat "$d/result.json")
+      case "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || echo malformed_response)" in
+        malformed_response|api_failure) st="failed"; _av_err=$(jq -r '.metadata.error // .metadata.status // ""' <<<"$res" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\000-\037\177' | cut -c1-200) ;;
+        *) st="succeeded"; res=$(_apply_hallucination_filter "$res" "$diff_file") ;;
+      esac
+    elif [[ "$(cat "$d/status" 2>/dev/null || true)" == "prompt_copy_failed" ]]; then st="failed"; _av_err="prompt_copy_failed"
+    else st="failed"; _av_err="the voice left no result"
+    fi
+    _av_rc=$(cat "$d/rc" 2>/dev/null || echo ""); [[ "$_av_rc" =~ ^[0-9]{1,3}$ ]] || _av_rc="null"
+    printf '%s' "$res" > "$d/block-in.json"
+    entry=$(jq -c -n --slurpfile cf "$counted" --slurpfile af "$d/block-in.json" --arg a "$_av_alias" --arg st "$st" --arg err "$_av_err" \
+      --argjson rc "$_av_rc" --argjson n "$_av_n" '
+      def anc: (.anchor // "") | if type == "string" then . else "" end;
+      def file: anc | split(":")[0];
+      def lines: ([anc | capture(":(?<a>[0-9]+)(-(?<b>[0-9]+))?$")] | .[0]) as $m
+        | if $m == null then null else ([($m.a | tonumber), (($m.b // $m.a) | tonumber)] | sort) end;
+      def overlaps($x; $y): if $x != null and $y != null then ($x[0] <= $y[1] and $y[0] <= $x[1]) else false end;
+      ($cf[0].findings // []) as $top
+      | ($af[0]) as $r
+      | (if $st == "succeeded" then ($r.findings // []) else [] end) as $fs
+      | {alias: $a, status: $st, counted_as: "advisory_voice",
+         findings: ($fs | to_entries | map(.value as $f
+           | ($f | file) as $ff | ($f | lines) as $fl | ($f | anc) as $fa
+           | ($top | map(select((file) == $ff and $ff != "" and ((.category // "") == ($f.category // ""))
+                                and (if (lines) != null and $fl != null then overlaps(lines; $fl) else (anc) == $fa end)))
+                   | (.[0].id // null)) as $dup
+           | $f + {id: ("DISS-A" + ($n | tostring) + "-" + ((.key + 1) | tostring | if length < 3 then ("000" + .)[-3:] else . end)),
+                   voice: "advisory", answered_by: $a, duplicate_of: $dup})),
+         rejected_count: ($r.metadata.rejected_count // 0), repaired_count: ($r.metadata.repaired_count // 0),
+         rejected_summary: ($r.metadata.rejected_summary // []),
+         cost_usd: ($r.metadata.cost_usd // 0), exit_code: $rc}
+        + (if $err == "" then {} else {error: $err} end)' 2>/dev/null) \
+      || entry=$(jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias" '{alias: $a, status: "failed", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [], error: "the advisory block could not be built"}')
+    printf '%s\n' "$entry" >> "$blk"
+    log "Advisory voice $_av_alias: $st ($(jq -r '.findings | length' <<<"$entry") finding(s), never counted)"
+  done
+  # the aliases refused by locality, named in the block too (never run)
+  local r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r
+  while IFS=$'\t' read -r r_role _av_alias_r _av_prov_r; do
+    [[ "$r_role" == "advisory" && -n "$_av_alias_r" ]] || continue
+    jq -cn --arg a "$_av_alias_r" --arg p "$_av_prov_r" '{alias: $a, status: "refused", counted_as: "advisory_voice", findings: [],
+      error: ("locality: local_voices refuses hosted hop " + $a + " (" + $p + ")")}' >> "$blk"
+  done <<<"$_ADV_LOC_REFUSED"
+  jq -cs '.' "$blk"
+}
+

+# cycle-129 FR-8 (SDD D-8.1, DEC-0146): hounfour.locality. Under local_voices the Flatline voices — primary, secondary,
+# tertiary, and so every scorer, since a voice cross-scores the others (no separate judge) — are planned only on a
+# provider whose model entry says `dispatch_group: local` in the merged config (lib/hop-locality.py: the catalog
+# overlaid with this config's hounfour.providers; a local entry whose fallback_chain reaches a hosted one is hosted).
+# A hosted voice is refused by name at plan time, never substituted: a hosted primary or secondary refuses the run (a
+# Flatline review needs both), a hosted tertiary is not planned (2-model mode). The advisor_strategy scorer route
+# (stage_routing.flatline_scorer) resolves its tier inside cheval, not as a declared hop, so it is refused too and the
+# scorers stay on the pinned voices. The red-team pipeline plans its own hops and is refused whole. cheval applies the
+# request-time rules to a local hop and records locality_mode / hop_locality in MODELINV from the same config key.
+_FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT=""   # "" not checked yet · ok · refused (memoised: main and run_phase1 both ask)
+flatline_locality_mode() {  # → hosted | local_voices | invalid:<value>
+    local tg v
+    [[ -f "$CONFIG_FILE" ]] && command -v yq >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "hosted"; return 0; }
+    tg=$(yq eval '.hounfour.locality | tag' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "unreadable")
+    case "$tg" in
+        '!!null'|'') echo "hosted" ;;
+        '!!str')
+            v=$(yq eval '.hounfour.locality' "$CONFIG_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo "")
+            case "$v" in hosted|local_voices) echo "$v" ;; *) echo "invalid:$(printf '%s' "$v" | LC_ALL=C tr -cd 'A-Za-z0-9._-' | cut -c1-40)" ;; esac ;;
+        *) echo "invalid:(a ${tg#!!}, not a string)" ;;
+    esac
+}
+flatline_locality_gate() {  # → 0 when the planned voices are allowed; 1 refused (said). Under local_voices a hosted tertiary
+                             # is dropped from the plan (the tertiary cache) and the advisor_strategy scorer route is turned off
+    case "$_FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT" in ok) return 0 ;; refused) return 1 ;; esac

+    if [[ "$mode" == hosted ]]; then _FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT=ok; return 0; fi
+    if [[ "$mode" == invalid:* ]]; then

+        _FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT=refused; return 1

+        --config "$CONFIG_FILE" -- "$p" "$s" ${t:+"$t"} 2>/dev/null) || rows=""
+    for role in primary secondary tertiary; do

+        _FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT=refused; return 1
+    fi
+    _FLATLINE_LOCALITY_RESULT=ok

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""hop-locality.py — classify model hops as local or hosted for `hounfour.locality: local_voices` (cycle-129 FR-8,
+SDD D-8.0 / D-8.1, DEC-0146).
+
+    python3 -I hop-locality.py --catalog <model-config.yaml> --config <.loa.config.yaml> -- <hop>...
+
+One tab-separated line per hop, in the order given:
+
+    <hop> TAB <provider|unknown> TAB <local|hosted> TAB <reason>
+
+A hop is `local` only when ALL of these hold in the merged view (the System Zone catalog overlaid with the project
+config's `hounfour.providers` / `hounfour.aliases`, the two layers cheval merges):
+  * it resolves (a `provider:id` pin, an alias chain, or a bare id that exactly one provider declares) to a model entry
+    that exists;
+  * that model entry, or its provider block, says `dispatch_group: local` (the canonical key, D-8.0);
+  * every hop on the entry's own `fallback_chain` is local by the same rule — cheval walks that chain inside one call,
+    so a local entry that falls back to a hosted one would leave the declared providers without the planner seeing it.
+Everything else is `hosted`: an unresolved hop, an unreadable config, a headless CLI hop (its dispatch group is the
+provider family's), the native session. Fail closed — a hop is never called local because it could not be read.
+
+This file reads declarations only: it never dispatches, never reads credentials and never imports the cheval package
+(run under `-I`, so neither the cwd nor PYTHONPATH reaches sys.path). The request-time rules for a local hop (IP-literal
+or localhost endpoint, no DNS, redirects refused, proxy env ignored, destination logged) are cheval's.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import argparse
+import sys
+from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
+
+MAX_DEPTH = 10
+
+
+def _merge(base: Any, overlay: Any) -> Any:
+    if isinstance(base, dict) and isinstance(overlay, dict):
+        out = dict(base)
+        for key, value in overlay.items():
+            out[key] = _merge(base.get(key), value) if key in base else value
+        return out
+    return overlay
+
+
+def load_merged(catalog_path: str, config_path: Optional[str]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
+    import yaml
+
+    with open(catalog_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+        catalog = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+    if not isinstance(catalog, dict):
+        raise ValueError("catalog is not a mapping")
+    merged: Dict[str, Any] = {k: (catalog.get(k) if isinstance(catalog.get(k), dict) else {})
+                              for k in ("providers", "aliases", "backward_compat_aliases")}
+    if config_path:
+        try:
+            with open(config_path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
+                project = yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}
+        except FileNotFoundError:
+            project = {}
+        if not isinstance(project, dict):
+            raise ValueError("project config is not a mapping")
+        hounfour = project.get("hounfour")
+        if isinstance(hounfour, dict):
+            for key in ("providers", "aliases"):
+                if isinstance(hounfour.get(key), dict):
+                    merged[key] = _merge(merged.get(key) or {}, hounfour[key])
+    return merged
+
+
+def _alias_target(name: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[str]:
+    for table in ("aliases", "backward_compat_aliases"):
+        target = (merged.get(table) or {}).get(name)
+        if isinstance(target, dict):
+            target = target.get("target") or target.get("model")
+        if isinstance(target, str) and target.strip():
+            return target.strip()
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Tuple[str, str]]:
+    name = (hop or "").strip()
+    if not name:
+        return None
+    current, seen = name, set()
+    for _ in range(MAX_DEPTH):
+        if ":" in current:
+            provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+            return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+        target = _alias_target(current, merged)
+        if not target:
+            break
+        if target in seen:
+            return None
+        seen.add(current)
+        current = target
+    if ":" in current:
+        provider, _, model = current.partition(":")
+        return (provider, model) if provider and model else None
+    providers = merged.get("providers") or {}
+    matches = [p for p, block in providers.items()
+               if isinstance(block, dict) and isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) and current in block["models"]]
+    return (matches[0], current) if len(matches) == 1 else None
+
+
+def classify(hop: str, merged: Dict[str, Any], _depth: int = 0, _seen: Optional[set] = None) -> Tuple[str, str, str]:
+    """(provider, locality, reason) for one hop."""
+    seen = set(_seen or ())
+    target = resolve(hop, merged)
+    if target is None:
+        return "unknown", "hosted", "unresolved"
+    provider, model = target
+    block = (merged.get("providers") or {}).get(provider)
+    if not isinstance(block, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "provider_not_declared"
+    entry = (block.get("models") or {}).get(model) if isinstance(block.get("models"), dict) else None
+    if not isinstance(entry, dict):
+        return provider, "hosted", "model_not_declared"
+    group = entry.get("dispatch_group") or block.get("dispatch_group") or ""
+    if group != "local":
+        return provider, "hosted", f"dispatch_group={group or 'unset'}"
+    key = f"{provider}:{model}"
+    if key in seen:
+        return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+    seen.add(key)
+    chain = entry.get("fallback_chain") or []
+    if not isinstance(chain, list):
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+    if _depth >= MAX_DEPTH:
+        return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_too_deep"
+    for nxt in chain:
+        if not isinstance(nxt, str):
+            return provider, "hosted", "fallback_chain_unreadable"
+        p2, loc, _ = classify(nxt, merged, _depth + 1, seen)
+        if loc != "local":
+            return provider, "hosted", f"fallback_chain_reaches_hosted:{nxt}({p2})"
+    return provider, "local", "dispatch_group=local"
+

+    return "".join(c if c.isprintable() and c not in "\t" else "_" for c in text)[:128]
+

+    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n")[0])
+    ap.add_argument("--catalog", required=True)
+    ap.add_argument("--config", default="")
+    ap.add_argument("hops", nargs="*")
+    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
+    try:
+        merged = load_merged(args.catalog, args.config or None)
+        err = ""
+    except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001 — fail closed: every hop hosted, the reason said once
+        merged, err = None, f"{type(exc).__name__}"
+        print(f"hop-locality: the merged config could not be read ({err}) — every hop is hosted", file=sys.stderr)
+    for hop in args.hops:
+        if merged is None:
+            print(f"{_clean(hop)}\tunknown\thosted\tconfig_unreadable")
+            continue
+        provider, loc, reason = classify(hop, merged)
+        print(f"{_clean(hop)}\t{_clean(provider)}\t{loc}\t{_clean(reason)}")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())

 fi
 
 # Fire BB with NO --pr: it self-discovers open PRs and dedups internally.
+# BB's stdout (its run JSON) is kept in the handoff dir and replayed, so a DEGRADED run can name its voices.
+BB_OUT="${HANDOFF_DIR}/bb-stdout.json"
 rc=0
 if [[ -x "$BB_ENTRY" ]]; then
-    "$BB_ENTRY" --repo "$repo" || rc=$?
+    "$BB_ENTRY" --repo "$repo" >"$BB_OUT" || rc=$?
 else
-    bash "$BB_ENTRY" --repo "$repo" || rc=$?
+    bash "$BB_ENTRY" --repo "$repo" >"$BB_OUT" || rc=$?
+fi
+cat "$BB_OUT"
+
+# cycle-129 D-7.7 (DEC-0150): exit 3 = the review COMPLETED with a DEGRADED consensus (bridgebuilder.exit_on_degraded;
+# 0 restores the old exit). Not a failure: one WARN naming the incomplete voices, `degraded: true` in the handoff, exit 0.
+degraded=false
+voices=""
+if [[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]]; then
+    degraded=true
+    voices=$(jq -r '[.verdicts[]?.voices.incomplete[]?] | unique | join(", ")' "$BB_OUT" 2>/dev/null) || voices=""
+    echo "dispatcher: WARN: bridgebuilder completed DEGRADED (exit 3): incomplete voices: ${voices:-none named (degraded verdict quality)}" >&2
 fi

-    --arg repo "$repo" --argjson ec "$rc" \
+    --arg repo "$repo" --argjson ec "$rc" --argjson degraded "$degraded" --arg voices "$voices" \
     '{cycle_id:$cid, schedule_id:$sid, dispatched:true, repo:$repo,
-      bb_exit_code:$ec}')"
+      bb_exit_code:$ec, degraded:$degraded}
+     + (if $degraded then {incomplete_voices: $voices} else {} end)')"
+if [[ "$rc" -eq 3 ]]; then
+    exit 0
+fi
 exit "$rc"

 # Hounfour Examples:
 #
+# Each example sits between a `# @example-begin <name>` and a `# @example-end`
+# marker. .claude/adapters/tests/test_config_examples_load.py uncomments every
+# marked block, merges it over the System defaults with the real cheval loader
+# and asserts it loads, so an example that would not load fails CI.
+#
 # Example 1: Conservative (all native, no remote calls)
+# The Claude Code session itself still runs against Anthropic.
+# @example-begin conservative
 # hounfour:
 #   flatline_routing: false
 #   agents:
@@ -1156,17 +1181,28 @@ hounfour:
 #       model: native
 #     flatline-reviewer:
 #       model: native
+# @example-end
 #
 # Example 2: Budget-conscious (lower daily limit, aggressive downgrade)
+# @example-begin budget-conscious
 # hounfour:
 #   metering:
 #     budget:
 #       daily_micro_usd: 50000000       # $50/day
 #       warn_at_percent: 60
 #       on_exceeded: block              # Hard stop instead of downgrade
+# @example-end
 #
 # Example 3: Custom provider (e.g., Azure OpenAI)
+# Every model of a custom HTTP provider declares endpoint_family, auth_type,
+# dispatch_group and context_window. The key is read from an environment
+# variable, which must match a secret_env_allowlist pattern: only LOA_*,
+# OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MOONSHOT_API_KEY, GOOGLE_API_KEY and
+# GEMINI_API_KEY are allowed by default.
+# @example-begin azure-openai
 # hounfour:
+#   secret_env_allowlist:
+#     - "^AZURE_OPENAI_KEY$"
 #   providers:
 #     azure-openai:
 #       type: openai
@@ -1174,12 +1210,57 @@ hounfour:
 #       auth: "{env:AZURE_OPENAI_KEY}"
 #       models:
 #         gpt-5-azure:
+#           endpoint_family: chat
+#           auth_type: http_api
+#           dispatch_group: azure
 #           capabilities: [chat, tools, function_calling]
+#           context_window: 400000
+#           max_output_tokens: 16000
 #           pricing:
 #             input_per_mtok: 10000000
 #             output_per_mtok: 30000000
 #   aliases:
 #     reviewer: "azure-openai:gpt-5-azure"
+# @example-end
+#
+# Example 4: Local OpenAI-compatible server (vLLM, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio)
+# Threat model: plain http is admitted only to the one host named in
+# allow_insecure_endpoint, an IP literal or localhost in a loopback or RFC1918
+# range that is never resolved through DNS, so the prompt does not cross a
+# public network unencrypted and the name cannot be rebound. For this provider
+# cheval ignores proxy environment variables, refuses redirects and keeps every
+# request under the declared endpoint path, while every other provider keeps the
+# https, loopback and private-range refusals.
+# keyless: true sends no credential (a literal auth: "local" means the same).
+# secret_env_allowlist: if your server does want a key, use
+# auth: "{env:LOCAL_LLM_KEY}" instead of keyless and add "^LOCAL_LLM_KEY$" to
+# secret_env_allowlist; an environment variable outside the allowlist is refused.
+# A prompt over the declared context_window refuses the hop by name and is never
+# truncated; the zero prices record the hop at cost 0.
+# @example-begin local-openai-compatible
+# hounfour:
+#   providers:
+#     local:
+#       type: openai_compat
+#       endpoint: "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1"
+#       keyless: true
+#       allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"   # a host string, never a boolean
+#       models:
+#         qwen3-coder-30b:
+#           endpoint_family: chat
+#           auth_type: http_api
+#           dispatch_group: local                # marks the hop local (hop_locality: local)
+#           capabilities: [chat]                 # add structured_json if the server enforces response_format
+#           context_window: 32768
+#           max_output_tokens: 8192
+#           streaming_recovery:
+#             first_token_deadline_s: 120        # CPU servers take a while on a large prompt
+#           pricing:
+#             input_per_mtok: 0
+#             output_per_mtok: 0
+#   aliases:
+#     local-reviewer: "local:qwen3-coder-30b"
+# @example-end
 trajectory:
   archive:
     # Maximum export size in MB before LFS warning
@@ -1591,6 +1672,17 @@ flatline_protocol:
     # and in the degraded-verdict trajectory record, so findings the
     # dissenter model produced but that were silently dropped for a
     # trivial schema mismatch (KF-004's original complaint) stay visible.
+    # cycle-129 FR-7: advisory voices (aliases — an open-weight or local model, say). They run after the counted
+    # voices on the same prompts, concurrently, under ONE wall clock (advisory_timeout_seconds), with the same schema,
+    # qualification and repair rules; their findings are written ONLY under advisory_voices[].findings in
+    # adversarial-review.json (voice: advisory, counted_as: advisory_voice, duplicate_of: the id of a counted finding
+    # on the same file, overlapping lines, same category) — never in findings[], voices_planned or verdict_quality, so
+    # they cannot change a verdict; a failed or timed-out one is a status in its entry. The budget gate prices every
+    # planned voice (primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory alias) at its catalog price, 10 / 30 USD per
+    # Mtok when the catalog has none (said by name). An alias also listed in companion_chain is refused at plan time:

+    advisory_timeout_seconds: 600

@@ -1603,6 +1695,8 @@ flatline_protocol:
     companion_voice: true        # cycle-126 FR-2.1: see code_review — with no route to the other family every audit is
                                  # DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW; false where one voice is the host's shape (an absent key is true);
                                  # a companion_chain is read per block — this block's own, as code_review documents it
+    advisory_voices: []          # cycle-129 FR-7: see code_review — findings under advisory_voices[] only, never tallied

   # Falls back to built-in resources/BEAUVOIR.md if file not found.
   persona_path: "grimoires/bridgebuilder/BEAUVOIR.md"

diff --git a/README.md b/README.md
index f9e6acb3..4d8fb07a 100644
--- a/README.md
+++ b/README.md
@@ -19,6 +19,18 @@ ## What's new in v2.0.0-rc.2 (release candidate)
 
 The 2.0 line ships as a **pre-release**: it soaks with real users, fixes land as `-rc.N`, and `2.0.0` is promoted once the exit criteria in the [rc.1 release notes](grimoires/loa/reports/release-notes-2.0.0-rc.1.md) are met. Stable users can stay on `v1.202.1` until then.
 
+**Unreleased — earned guards and open voices** (cycle-129, [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)):
+
+- **Every guard carries its origin and its yield**: `grimoires/loa/guards.md` lists every hook, fence pattern, validator rule and gate with where it came from and whether it is active, dormant or telemetry; `.run/guard-yield.json` counts its real blocks and likely false positives over 30 days; `/loa` prints a Guards line. `guard-yield.sh --check` fails CI when a guard has no origin.
+- **Control arms**: the recall evals can run with a kernel block, the companion voice or the rule files switched off (`run-arms.sh`), against a record corpus of eight real sprints, so a rule's claim on review recall is measured before its text is cut. The kernel kept every pinned rationale this cycle (the arm run was still running at the gate) and shrank by the Agent Teams table; its byte cap fell to 9,445 B.
+- **Controls that run or go**: `implement_gate.mode` (`ask`, the default, logs a row; `telemetry`; `deny` refuses an unsanctioned App-Zone write while the run position is known), run position derived from files (`run-checkpoint.sh derive`), the circuit breaker as a script (`record-round`), per-task surgical-diff state; the input guardrails and danger-level enforcement default off in the example (82 events, zero catches), the Agent Teams rules live in their reference, and the pure-review skills carry `disallowed-tools`.
+- **The fence stops blocking prose**: a heredoc whose consumer only writes a file (`cat`, `tee`, `gh pr comment -F -`, `git commit -F -`, …) is scanned per segment, not as a command; interpreters, wrappers, substitutions, executable targets and anything unlisted still scan in full (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier`, corpus 99 benign / 184 dangerous rows). Two pre-existing holes closed on the way: a backtick substitution was inert to every rule, and `gh api` with a destructive method on refs, branch protection, tags, releases or the repository had no rule (`FR-GH-1`).
+- **One profile knob**: `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` sets the nine optional surfaces; no floor key is reachable through it; the example ships those keys as commented, profile-governed lines so a copied example follows the profile you choose, and `/loa` says when a guardrail control is off.
+- **Task kinds**: every sprint task says whether it is mechanical, judgment or operator work, and `tools/cycle-ratio.sh` prints the cycle's script / prose / model-call ratio.
+- **Open voices**: a local OpenAI-compatible server is a declared provider (`keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"`; one endpoint rule in cheval, the bash validator and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>`), the chat path sends `response_format` json_schema and strips thinking traces honestly, `advisory_voices` run beside the dissent's counted voices and can never change a verdict, and `hounfour.locality: local_voices` refuses every hosted hop by name across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the probe. Bridgebuilder reads providers only from trusted configuration, prints `completed/planned` voices and exits 3 on a degraded consensus.
+
+Upgrading: see the CHANGELOG Migration notes — `implement_gate.mode: ask` and `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false` are the rollback keys; set `guardrails.input.enabled: true` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` (or `loa.profile: full`) to restore the old guardrail defaults.
+
 **Unreleased — decision surfaces** (cycle-128, [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)):
 
 - **Decision maps**: `/chart <slug>` maps an effort that spans more than one cycle as `question` tickets and a map doc in `grimoires/loa/maps/`. It plans and never builds, and `/plan` reports the `charting` phase.

 The 2.0 line ships as a **pre-release**: it soaks with real users, fixes land as `-rc.N`, and `2.0.0` is promoted once the exit criteria in the [rc.1 release notes](grimoires/loa/reports/release-notes-2.0.0-rc.1.md) are met. Stable users can stay on `v1.202.1` until then.
 
+**Unreleased — earned guards and open voices** (cycle-129, [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)):
+
+- **Every guard carries its origin and its yield**: `grimoires/loa/guards.md` lists every hook, fence pattern, validator rule and gate with where it came from and whether it is active, dormant or telemetry; `.run/guard-yield.json` counts its real blocks and likely false positives over 30 days; `/loa` prints a Guards line. `guard-yield.sh --check` fails CI when a guard has no origin.
+- **Control arms**: the recall evals can run with a kernel block, the companion voice or the rule files switched off (`run-arms.sh`), against a record corpus of eight real sprints, so a rule's claim on review recall is measured before its text is cut. The kernel kept every pinned rationale this cycle (the arm run was still running at the gate) and shrank by the Agent Teams table; its byte cap fell to 9,445 B.
+- **Controls that run or go**: `implement_gate.mode` (`ask`, the default, logs a row; `telemetry`; `deny` refuses an unsanctioned App-Zone write while the run position is known), run position derived from files (`run-checkpoint.sh derive`), the circuit breaker as a script (`record-round`), per-task surgical-diff state; the input guardrails and danger-level enforcement default off in the example (82 events, zero catches), the Agent Teams rules live in their reference, and the pure-review skills carry `disallowed-tools`.
+- **The fence stops blocking prose**: a heredoc whose consumer only writes a file (`cat`, `tee`, `gh pr comment -F -`, `git commit -F -`, …) is scanned per segment, not as a command; interpreters, wrappers, substitutions, executable targets and anything unlisted still scan in full (`destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier`, corpus 99 benign / 184 dangerous rows). Two pre-existing holes closed on the way: a backtick substitution was inert to every rule, and `gh api` with a destructive method on refs, branch protection, tags, releases or the repository had no rule (`FR-GH-1`).
+- **One profile knob**: `loa.profile: lean | standard | full` sets the nine optional surfaces; no floor key is reachable through it; the example ships those keys as commented, profile-governed lines so a copied example follows the profile you choose, and `/loa` says when a guardrail control is off.
+- **Task kinds**: every sprint task says whether it is mechanical, judgment or operator work, and `tools/cycle-ratio.sh` prints the cycle's script / prose / model-call ratio.
+- **Open voices**: a local OpenAI-compatible server is a declared provider (`keyless: true`, `allow_insecure_endpoint: "127.0.0.1"`; one endpoint rule in cheval, the bash validator and `model-health-probe.sh --provider <name>`), the chat path sends `response_format` json_schema and strips thinking traces honestly, `advisory_voices` run beside the dissent's counted voices and can never change a verdict, and `hounfour.locality: local_voices` refuses every hosted hop by name across the dissent, Flatline, Bridgebuilder and the probe. Bridgebuilder reads providers only from trusted configuration, prints `completed/planned` voices and exits 3 on a degraded consensus.
+
+Upgrading: see the CHANGELOG Migration notes — `implement_gate.mode: ask` and `destructive_command_guard.heredoc_classifier: false` are the rollback keys; set `guardrails.input.enabled: true` and `guardrails.danger_level.enforce: true` (or `loa.profile: full`) to restore the old guardrail defaults.
+
 **Unreleased — decision surfaces** (cycle-128, [CHANGELOG](CHANGELOG.md)):
 
 - **Decision maps**: `/chart <slug>` maps an effort that spans more than one cycle as `question` tickets and a map doc in `grimoires/loa/maps/`. It plans and never builds, and `/plan` reports the `charting` phase.

diff --git a/tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats b/tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats

index 00000000..ca697488
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,198 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-advisory.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.3, SDD D-7.4, DEC-0165, DEC-0155).
+#
+# Advisory voices run after the counted voices on the same prompts, concurrently, under one wall clock; their findings
+# live ONLY under advisory_voices[].findings (voice: advisory, counted_as: advisory_voice, duplicate_of links); the rest of
+# the envelope and the verdict-derive output are byte-identical (normalised: timestamps removed) with and without them;
+# a failed or timed-out advisory voice is a status, never a verdict input; an attempt to count one is refused by name.
+# Mock mode: invoke_dissenter is the harness stub (tests/unit/adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash) — no model is called.
+# =============================================================================
+
+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
+
+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3adv; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
+
+_base_cfg() {  # [extra lines for the code_review block]
+    s3_config "flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: gpt-5.5-pro
+    budget_cents: 500
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    fallback_chain: []
+${1:-}"
+}
+
+_feedback() {  # an approved review next to the envelope, for verdict-derive
+    mkdir -p "$OUT_DIR"
+    printf '%s\n' 'All good' '' 'No issues found.' \
+      '<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"gate":"review","verdict":"APPROVED","counts":{"critical":0,"high":0,"medium":0,"low":0},"sprint_id":"sprint-x","ts":"2026-10-14T00:00:00Z"} -->' \
+      > "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md"
+}
+
+_vd() {  # → verdict-derive's --json output on the standing envelope (status recorded, output kept whatever it is)
+    "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/verdict-derive.sh" --file "$OUT_DIR/engineer-feedback.md" --gate review --json 2>"$T/vd.err" || true
+}
+
+@test "ADV-1 an advisory voice's findings are present only under advisory_voices[].findings, tagged and linked by duplicate_of" {
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two]"
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    # the counted voices are untouched: primary + companion, nothing advisory at the top level
+    [ "$(jq '.findings | length' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.findings[] | select(.voice == "advisory")] | length' "$env")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    # the block
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$env")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].alias' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].counted_as' "$env")" = "advisory_voice" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices[0].findings | length' "$env")" = "3" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].voice] | unique | join(",")' "$env")" = "advisory" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[0].findings[].id] | join(",")' "$env")" = "DISS-A1-001,DISS-A1-002,DISS-A1-003" ]
+    # same file, overlapping lines (9-12 over 10), same category → the counted primary finding; else null
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "DISS-001" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[1].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (line 40: no overlap)
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[2].duplicate_of' "$env")" = "null" ]   # (same line, another category)
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].findings[0].answered_by' "$env")" = "adv-two" ]
+    grep -qx "adv-two" "$CALLS"
+    # stdout carries the same envelope
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' <<<"$result")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-2 the envelope without advisory_voices and the verdict-derive --json output are byte-identical with and without advisory voices" {
+    _feedback
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two; BEHAVIOUR[adv-reject]=reject; BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail
+    _base_cfg
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/without.json"
+    _vd > "$T/vd-without.json"
+    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-without"
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-two, adv-reject, adv-fail]"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    cp "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" "$T/with.json"
+    _vd > "$T/vd-with.json"
+    ls "$OUT_DIR" | LC_ALL=C sort > "$T/ls-with"
+    [ "$(jq '.advisory_voices | length' "$T/with.json")" = "3" ]
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$T/without.json" >/dev/null
+    # the normalised envelopes (advisory_voices deleted, timestamps removed, keys sorted) are byte-identical
+    diff <(s3_norm "$T/without.json") <(s3_norm "$T/with.json")
+    # …and each named input on its own, so a failure names it
+    local k
+    for k in '.findings' '.verdict_quality' '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded' \
+             '.metadata.companion_voice' '.metadata.rejected_summary' '.metadata.rejected_sidecars' '.metadata.cost_usd'; do
+        [ "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/without.json")" = "$(jq -cS "$k" "$T/with.json")" ] || { echo "differs: $k"; return 1; }
+    done
+    # verdict-derive reads the same envelope and sidecars: its --json output is byte-identical
+    [ -s "$T/vd-without.json" ]
+    diff "$T/vd-without.json" "$T/vd-with.json"
+    # the advisory voice's rejected payload never landed beside the envelope (verdict-derive would count it)
+    diff "$T/ls-without" "$T/ls-with"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[] | select(.alias == "adv-reject") | .rejected_count' "$T/with.json")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-3 a failed or malformed advisory voice is recorded under advisory_voices[].status and ignored by verdict quality" {
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-fail]=fail; BEHAVIOUR[adv-bad]=malformed
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-fail, adv-bad]"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.advisory_voices[].status] | join(",")' "$env")" = "failed,failed" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.advisory_voices[].findings | length] | add' "$env")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.verdict_quality.status' "$env")" = "APPROVED" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_succeeded' "$env")" = "2" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.verdict_quality.voices_dropped[]?.voice] | map(select(test("adv-"))) | length' "$env")" = "0" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-4 the advisory wall clock is honoured: a voice still running is killed and timed_out while a fast one completes" {
+    BEHAVIOUR[adv-slow]=slow; BEHAVIOUR[adv-two]=two
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [adv-slow, adv-two]
+    advisory_timeout_seconds: 2"
+    local t0 t1; t0=$(date +%s)
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    t1=$(date +%s)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    (( t1 - t0 < 60 ))
+    env="$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[0].status' "$env")" = "timed_out" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.advisory_voices[1].status' "$env")" = "succeeded" ]
+    grep -q "Advisory voice adv-slow: still running at the 2s advisory wall clock — killed (timed_out)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    # the hung hop did not outlive the run
+    sleep 0.5
+    ! pgrep -f "loa-s3adv-slow-$$" >/dev/null || { echo "the hung advisory hop outlived the run"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq '.verdict_quality.voices_planned' "$env")" = "2" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-5 an advisory alias the block also counts in companion_chain is refused by name at plan time, before any call" {
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: [claude-headless]
+    companion_chain:
+      anthropic: [claude-headless]"
+    printf 'hounfour:\n  advisory_promotion:\n    min_recall_ratio: 0.8\n' >> "$CONFIG_FILE"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "1" ]
+    grep -qF "advisory voice claude-headless cannot be counted: no arms report line for the alias (voice arms are a future iteration)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "hounfour.advisory_promotion: min_recall_ratio=0.8, max_refuted_delta=unset" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "advisory_promotion_refused" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.alias' <<<"$result")" = "claude-headless" ]
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+    [ ! -e "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" ]
+}
+
+@test "ADV-6 with no advisory_voices the envelope has no advisory_voices key (the default is unchanged)" {
+    _base_cfg
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" >/dev/null
+    _base_cfg "    advisory_voices: []"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    jq -e 'has("advisory_voices") | not' "$OUT_DIR/adversarial-review.json" >/dev/null

+}
+

+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-budget.bats — cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.3 (PRD FR-7 AC-7.5, SDD D-7.4, D-7.6).
+#
+# The dissent budget pre-check prices every planned voice — the primary, the companion's first hop, each advisory voice —
+# at its catalog price (python3 -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias), instead of the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok.
+# An alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 for that voice and is said by name; a zero-priced entry estimates
+# zero and is said too. Prices come from fixture entries in the test's project config (hounfour.providers overlays the
+# catalog, as cheval merges it). Each voice: input tokens × input rate + 2000 × output rate, micro-USD/Mtok → cents.
+# =============================================================================
+
+load adversarial-review-s3-helpers
+
+setup() { export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"; s3_setup sprint-s3bud; }   # (the CLI lock is this test's own — CMP-121)
+teardown() { s3_teardown; }
+
+_cfg() {  # <model> <budget> <companion_voice> [extra code_review lines]
+    s3_config "hounfour:
+  providers:
+    openai:
+      models:
+        fixture-priced:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 2000000, output_per_mtok: 8000000}
+    fixturelocal:
+      models:
+        fixture-zero:
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 0, output_per_mtok: 0}
+        fixture-stale:
+          price_date: \"2000-01-01\"
+          pricing: {input_per_mtok: 1000000, output_per_mtok: 1000000}
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:
+    enabled: true
+    model: $1
+    budget_cents: $2
+    timeout_seconds: 30
+    companion_voice: $3
+    fallback_chain: []
+${4:-}"
+}
+
+_big_diff() {  # a diff whose estimate is 1,000,500 input tokens (3,000,000 bytes / 3 + 500)
+    { printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n'; head -c $(( 3000000 - 25 )) /dev/zero | tr '\0' 'a'; } > "$T/diff.patch"
+    [ "$(wc -c < "$T/diff.patch")" -eq 3000000 ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-1 the primary is priced at its catalog rate (no fixed-rate fallback): 1,000,500 tokens × 2 + 2000 × 8 USD/Mtok = 201c" {
+    _big_diff
+    _cfg fixture-priced 150 false
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.status' <<<"$result")" = "budget_exceeded" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "201" ]
+    [ "$(jq -c '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | {role, alias, estimated_cents, pricing_source}]' <<<"$result")" = '[{"role":"primary","alias":"fixture-priced","estimated_cents":201,"pricing_source":"config"}]' ]
+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 201c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-priced 201c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    ! grep -q "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log" || { echo "a catalog-priced primary fell back"; return 1; }
+    [ ! -s "$CALLS" ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-2 an alias with no catalog price falls back to 10 / 30 USD per Mtok for that voice, said by name (1000c + 6c)" {
+    _big_diff
+    _cfg mystery-model-x 150 false
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.metadata.estimate_voices[0].pricing_source' <<<"$result")" = "fallback" ]
+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (primary) — the fixed 10 / 30 USD per Mtok applies to this voice" "$T/stderr.log"
+    [ "$(grep -c "no catalog price" "$T/stderr.log")" = "1" ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-3 a zero-priced entry estimates 0c and is said: a 0-cent budget admits it, where the fixed rate would refuse" {
+    _cfg fixture-zero 0 false
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (primary) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "budget: estimate 0c over 1 planned voice(s) (primary fixture-zero 0c)" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qx "fixture-zero" "$CALLS"
+    # the same run priced at the fixed rate is refused (the regression this replaces: 2000 output tokens × 30 = 6c > 0)
+    _cfg mystery-model-x 0 false
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ]
+}
+
+@test "BUD-4 the gate sums every planned voice: primary + the companion's first hop + each advisory voice" {
+    _big_diff
+    _cfg fixture-priced 1 true "    advisory_voices: [fixture-zero, mystery-model-x]"
+    result=$(s3_run review)
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "4" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    [ "$(jq -r '[.metadata.estimate_voices[] | "\(.role)=\(.alias)"] | join(" ")' <<<"$result")" = "primary=fixture-priced companion=claude-headless advisory=fixture-zero advisory=mystery-model-x" ]
+    # the companion's price is the catalog's (whatever it is today): recompute it from the same CLI
+    local row ci co comp
+    row=$(PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters" python3 -W ignore::RuntimeWarning -m loa_cheval.metering.pricing --alias claude-headless --config "$CONFIG_FILE")
+    ci=$(sed -n 's/.* input_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row"); co=$(sed -n 's/.* output_per_mtok=\([0-9]*\) .*/\1/p' <<<"$row")
+    [[ "$ci" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$co" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]
+    comp=$(( 1000500 * ci / 10000000000 + 2000 * co / 10000000000 ))
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[1].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$comp" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[2].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "0" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimate_voices[3].estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "1006" ]
+    [ "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" = "$(( 201 + comp + 0 + 1006 ))" ]
+    [ "$(jq '[.metadata.estimate_voices[].estimated_cents] | add' <<<"$result")" = "$(jq '.metadata.estimated_cents' <<<"$result")" ]
+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-zero (advisory) is zero-priced in the catalog — estimated 0c" "$T/stderr.log"
+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for mystery-model-x (advisory)" "$T/stderr.log"
+}
+
+@test "BUD-5 a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) is used as given and said" {
+    _cfg fixture-stale 1000 false
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ] || { cat "$T/stderr.log"; return 1; }
+    grep -qF "budget: fixture-stale (primary) has a stale catalog price (price_date older than 90 days) — used as given" "$T/stderr.log"
+}
+
+@test "BUD-6 with no price CLI answer at all every voice falls back and is said (the gate never prices from nothing)" {
+    _cfg fixture-priced 1000 false
+    # a PYTHONPATH that cannot import the package: the CLI fails, every planned voice is unknown
+    local real patched
+    real="$(declare -f _adv_budget_estimate)"
+    patched="${real/PYTHONPATH=\"\$PROJECT_ROOT\/.claude\/adapters\"/PYTHONPATH=/nonexistent}"
+    [ "$patched" != "$real" ]   # (the seam was found: the CLI really cannot be imported in this run)
+    eval "$patched"
+    s3_run review >/dev/null
+    [ "$(cat "$T/rc")" = "0" ]
+    grep -qF "budget: no catalog price for fixture-priced (primary)" "$T/stderr.log"
+}

+# chain is the answering voice). With one local family the audit is DEGRADED_SECURITY_REVIEW, the gate and verdict-derive
+# treat the envelope as today, and the output says so. The default (hosted) is unchanged. Mock mode: the harness stub.
+# =============================================================================

+# one hosted provider (openai, the catalog's) and one local provider (localbox, declared here)

+    s3_config "hounfour:
+$loc
+  providers:
+    localbox:

+      endpoint: \"http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1\"

+          dispatch_group: local

+          dispatch_group: local
+          fallback_chain: [\"openai:gpt-5.5\"]

+    lq: \"localbox:qwen-local\"
+    lqb: \"localbox:qwen-local-b\"
+    lqc: \"localbox:qwen-local-c\"
+flatline_protocol:
+  code_review:

+_hosted_in() {  # <file of hop names, one per line> → the hosted ones, as hop-locality.py classifies them against this config
+    local hops; hops=$(sed 's/^repair://' "$1" | sort -u | grep -v '^$' || true)
+    [[ -n "$hops" ]] || return 0
+    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
+    python3 -I "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib/hop-locality.py" --catalog "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/defaults/model-config.yaml" \

+# shellcheck shell=bash
+# =============================================================================
+# tests/unit/adversarial-review-s3-helpers.bash — the whole-run harness shared by the cycle-129 Sprint 3 suites
+# (adversarial-review-advisory.bats, -budget.bats, -locality.bats).
+#
+# main() is sourced and run with `invoke_dissenter` replaced by a stub keyed on the model (canned adapter envelopes + a
+# valid single-voice verdict_quality sidecar, the shape the companion suite uses), a temp .loa.config.yaml, a temp
+# catalog when a case needs one, no credentials (a keyless host) and the test's own ledgers. No model is ever called.
+# =============================================================================
+
+s3_setup() {  # <sprint prefix>
+    umask 022
+    S3_PREFIX="$1"
+    SPRINT="${S3_PREFIX}-$$-${BATS_TEST_NUMBER:-0}"
+    : "${BATS_TEST_TMPDIR:?BATS_TEST_TMPDIR not set — needs bats-core >= 1.4}"
+    T="$BATS_TEST_TMPDIR"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIRNAME/../.." && pwd)"
+    export PROJECT_ROOT
+    OUT_DIR="$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/$SPRINT"
+    [[ ! -e "$OUT_DIR" && ! -L "$OUT_DIR" ]] || { echo "setup: $OUT_DIR already stands" >&2; SPRINT=""; return 1; }
+    export LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH="$T/model-invoke.jsonl"
+    export LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH="$T/cost-ledger.jsonl"
+    export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR="$T" XDG_CACHE_HOME="$T/xdg-cache"
+    export TMPDIR="$T/tmp"; mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
+    unset LOA_ADVERSARIAL_KEEP_WORKDIR LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_TAG LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REJECT_SIDECAR_DISABLE \
+          LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_MODEL LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REAP_GRACE_SECONDS LOA_MODEL_CONFIG LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_HOP_TIMEOUT \
+          LOA_ADVERSARIAL_NO_FM_DERIVATION LOA_ADVERSARIAL_RUN_LOCK_GRACE_SECONDS LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REPAIR_BUDGET_SECONDS \
+          LOA_ADVERSARIAL_DISABLE_FALLBACK LOA_ADVERSARIAL_COMPANION_WAIT_SECONDS _ADV_PGREP_BIN _ADV_FLOCK_BIN _ADV_REDACTOR_BIN
+    local saved_root="$PROJECT_ROOT" _src
+    source "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/lib-content.sh"
+    source "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"
+    _src="$(sed 's/^\( *\)main "\$@"$/\1: main disabled for testing/' "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/adversarial-review.sh")"
+    grep -q ': main disabled for testing' <<<"$_src" || { echo "setup: the main trailer sed matched nothing" >&2; return 1; }
+    eval "$_src"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$saved_root"; export PROJECT_ROOT
+    local p v; local -a row
+    for p in anthropic openai google; do read -ra row <<<"$(_adv_cred_aliases "$p")"; for v in "${row[@]}"; do unset "$v"; done; done
+    export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_ENV_DIR="$T/env"; mkdir -p "$LOA_ADVERSARIAL_ENV_DIR"
+    if _adv_cred_present anthropic || _adv_cred_present openai; then echo "setup: a credential alias is still present" >&2; return 1; fi
+    export LOA_ADVERSARIAL_CLI_PROBE=both
+    CONFIG_FILE="$T/loa.config.yaml"
+    printf 'diff --git a/x.sh b/x.sh\n--- a/x.sh\n+++ b/x.sh\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-a\n+b\n' > "$T/diff.patch"
+    CALLS="$T/calls.log"; : > "$CALLS"
+    declare -gA BEHAVIOUR=()
+    # the repair round-trip is not under test here: every repair is unavailable (the payload stays rejected)
+    _repair_finding_via_model() { return 1; }
+    invoke_dissenter() {  # <sys> <user> <model> <timeout> <vq_sidecar> <type> [schema]
+        local model="$3" sidecar="$5" b sev="ADVISORY"
+        [[ "${6:-review}" == "audit" ]] && sev="MEDIUM"   # each gate's own vocabulary — no reject detour
+        echo "$model" >> "$CALLS"
+        b="${BEHAVIOUR[$model]:-ok}"
+        case "$b" in
+            ok)
+                [[ -n "$sidecar" ]] && _s3_vq "$model" ok > "$sidecar"
+                jq -nc --arg m "$model" --arg s "$sev" \
+                  '{content: ({findings: [{id: "DISS-001", severity: $s, category: "error-handling", anchor: "x.sh:10",
+                     description: ("from " + $m + "."), failure_mode: "fm"}]} | tojson),
+                    tokens_input: 100, tokens_output: 20, cost_usd: 0.0123, latency_ms: 5, schema_enforced: false}'
+                return 0 ;;
+            two)   # one finding that matches the counted one (same file, overlapping lines, same category), one on another line,
+                   # one on the same line in another category
+                [[ -n "$sidecar" ]] && _s3_vq "$model" ok > "$sidecar"
+                jq -nc --arg m "$model" --arg s "$sev" '{content: ({findings: [
+                    {id: "DISS-001", severity: $s, category: "error-handling", anchor: "x.sh:9-12", description: ("dup from " + $m + "."), failure_mode: "fm"},
+                    {id: "DISS-002", severity: $s, category: "error-handling", anchor: "x.sh:40", description: ("new from " + $m + "."), failure_mode: "fm"},
+                    {id: "DISS-003", severity: $s, category: "performance", anchor: "x.sh:10", description: ("other category from " + $m + "."), failure_mode: "fm"}]} | tojson),
+                    tokens_input: 100, tokens_output: 20, cost_usd: 0.002, latency_ms: 5, schema_enforced: false}'
+                return 0 ;;
+            reject)   # a payload the normaliser cannot save (no severity)
+                [[ -n "$sidecar" ]] && _s3_vq "$model" ok > "$sidecar"
+                jq -nc '{content: "{\"findings\":[{\"title\":\"no severity\",\"category\":\"other\",\"description\":\"Something fails.\"}]}", tokens_input: 5, tokens_output: 5, cost_usd: 0.001, latency_ms: 1, schema_enforced: false}'
+                return 0 ;;
+            fail)  [[ -n "$sidecar" ]] && _s3_vq "$model" fail ProviderUnavailable 1 > "$sidecar"; return 1 ;;
+            malformed) [[ -n "$sidecar" ]] && _s3_vq "$model" ok > "$sidecar"; jq -nc '{content: "not json", tokens_input: 1, tokens_output: 1, cost_usd: 0, latency_ms: 1, schema_enforced: false}'; return 0 ;;
+            slow)  bash -c 'exec -a "$0" sleep 300' "loa-s3adv-slow-$$"; return 0 ;;
+            *) echo "stub: no arm for '$b'" >&2; return 99 ;;
+        esac
+    }
+    _s3_vq() {  # <voice> <ok|fail> [reason] [exit]
+        if [[ "$2" == ok ]]; then
+            jq -nc --arg v "$1" '{status:"APPROVED",consensus_outcome:"consensus",truncation_waiver_applied:false,voices_planned:1,voices_succeeded:1,voices_succeeded_ids:[$v],voices_dropped:[],chain_health:"ok",confidence_floor:"low",rationale:"stub",single_voice_call:true}'
+        else
+            jq -nc --arg v "$1" --arg r "$3" --argjson e "$4" '{status:"FAILED",consensus_outcome:"consensus",truncation_waiver_applied:false,voices_planned:1,voices_succeeded:0,voices_succeeded_ids:[],voices_dropped:[{voice:$v,reason:$r,exit_code:$e,blocker_risk:"unknown"}],chain_health:"exhausted",confidence_floor:"low",rationale:"stub",single_voice_call:true}'
+        fi
+    }
+    export PYTHONPATH="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/adapters"
+}
+
+s3_teardown() {
+    pkill -KILL -f "loa-s3adv-slow-$$"'( |$)' 2>/dev/null || true
+    [[ -n "${SPRINT:-}" && "$SPRINT" == "${S3_PREFIX:-x}"-* && -n "${PROJECT_ROOT:-}" ]] || return 0
+    local d="$PROJECT_ROOT/grimoires/loa/a2a/$SPRINT"
+    if [[ -d "$d" && ! -L "$d" ]]; then find "$d" -mindepth 1 -delete; rmdir "$d"; fi
+    return 0
+}
+
+s3_config() {  # <yaml body> → the test's .loa.config.yaml (owner-only)
+    printf '%s\n' "$1" > "$CONFIG_FILE"
+}
+
+s3_run() {  # <review|audit> → main's stdout (main runs in a subshell: it exits); stderr to $T/stderr.log; the status in $T/rc
+    local rc=0
+    ( main --type "${1:-review}" --sprint-id "$SPRINT" --diff-file "$T/diff.patch" --json ) 2> "$T/stderr.log" || rc=$?
+    printf '%s' "$rc" > "$T/rc"
+}
+
+s3_norm() {  # <envelope file> → the envelope without advisory_voices, keys sorted, and only the clock-dependent fields removed
+    # (the normalised compare: a timestamp and the repairs' measured wall seconds differ between any two runs, advisory or not)
+    jq -S 'del(.advisory_voices) | walk(if type == "object" then del(.timestamp, .ts_utc, .repair_wall_seconds) else . end)' "$1"
+}
diff --git a/tests/unit/bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats b/tests/unit/bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..2929ee1e
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/unit/bb-exit-degraded-callers.bats
@@ -0,0 +1,130 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bats
+# cycle-129 Sprint 3 Task 3.4 (SDD D-7.7, DEC-0150): Bridgebuilder exits 3 when a multi-model review COMPLETED with a
+# DEGRADED consensus. Every shell caller that tests the exit code treats 3 as "completed, degraded": one WARN line naming
+# the incomplete voices, never a failure. A stub Bridgebuilder entry.sh stands in for the real one.
+
+setup() {
+    BATS_TEST_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "$BATS_TEST_FILENAME")" && pwd)"
+    PROJECT_ROOT="$(cd "$BATS_TEST_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
+    WORK="$(mktemp -d "${BATS_TMPDIR:-/tmp}/bb-exit-degraded.XXXXXX")"
+    STUB="$WORK/stub-entry.sh"
+}
+
+teardown() {
+    [[ -n "${WORK:-}" && -d "$WORK" ]] && rm -rf "$WORK"
+}
+
+# make_stub <exit_code>: a stub entry.sh that prints a run JSON naming one incomplete voice, then exits <exit_code>
+make_stub() {
+    cat > "$STUB" <<'STUB_EOF'
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+echo '{"mode":"multi-model","degraded":true,"verdicts":[{"pr":7,"voices":{"planned":2,"completed":1,"incomplete":["openai/gpt-5.5"]}}]}'
+STUB_EOF
+    echo "exit $1" >> "$STUB"
+    chmod +x "$STUB"
+}
+
+# --- session-cap-bb dispatcher.sh ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+run_dispatcher() {
+    local cid="cyc-$1"
+    local handoff="$WORK/tmp/loa-session-cap-bb.$cid"
+    mkdir -p "$handoff"
+    printf '{"action":"dispatch"}' > "$handoff/decider.json"
+    DISPATCHER_JSON="$handoff/dispatcher.json"
+    run env TMPDIR="$WORK/tmp" LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_ENTRY="$STUB" LOA_SESSION_CAP_BB_REPO="fixture/repo" \
+        bash "$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/scheduled-cycle-template/contracts/session-cap-bb/dispatcher.sh" "$cid" sched-1 0 '[]'
+}
+
+@test "dispatcher: Bridgebuilder exit 3 is completed-degraded — WARN names the voice, handoff degraded, exit 0" {
+    make_stub 3
+    run_dispatcher a
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: bridgebuilder completed DEGRADED (exit 3): incomplete voices: openai/gpt-5.5"* ]]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.bb_exit_code' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "3" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.degraded' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "true" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.incomplete_voices' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "openai/gpt-5.5" ]
+}
+
+@test "dispatcher: Bridgebuilder's run JSON still reaches stdout" {
+    make_stub 3
+    run_dispatcher b
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *'"mode":"multi-model"'* ]]
+}
+
+@test "dispatcher: exit 0 stays 0 with degraded false and no WARN" {
+    make_stub 0
+    run_dispatcher c
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"DEGRADED"* ]]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.degraded' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "false" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r 'has("incomplete_voices")' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+@test "dispatcher: any other non-zero exit is still a failure" {
+    make_stub 1
+    run_dispatcher d
+    [ "$status" -eq 1 ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.bb_exit_code' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "1" ]
+    [ "$(jq -r '.degraded' "$DISPATCHER_JSON")" = "false" ]
+}
+
+# --- spiral-harness.sh _gate_bridgebuilder ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# run_gate <exit_code>: source the harness, point it at a fake skills tree holding the stub, run the gate
+run_gate() {
+    make_stub "$1"
+    mkdir -p "$WORK/fake/scripts" "$WORK/fake/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources" "$WORK/evidence"
+    cp "$STUB" "$WORK/fake/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/entry.sh"
+    run bash -c '
+        cd "$1" || exit 99
+        source "$2/.claude/scripts/spiral-harness.sh"
+        set +e
+        SCRIPT_DIR="$1/fake/scripts"
+        EVIDENCE_DIR="$1/evidence"
+        _record_action() { echo "RECORDED:$1:${10}"; }
+        _gate_bridgebuilder "https://github.com/fixture/repo/pull/7"
+        echo "GATE_RC=$?"
+    ' _ "$WORK" "$PROJECT_ROOT"
+}
+
+@test "spiral-harness gate: Bridgebuilder exit 3 logs one WARN naming the voice and the gate passes" {
+    run_gate 3
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: Bridgebuilder review iter 1 completed DEGRADED (exit 3): incomplete voices: openai/gpt-5.5"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"RECORDED:GATE_BRIDGEBUILDER:posted"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"GATE_RC=0"* ]]
+    [ "$(grep -c 'DEGRADED' <<<"$output")" -eq 1 ]
+}
+
+@test "spiral-harness gate: exit 0 logs no WARN" {
+    run_gate 0
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" != *"WARN: Bridgebuilder"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"GATE_RC=0"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "spiral-harness gate: another non-zero exit is logged as not completed (non-blocking, as before)" {
+    run_gate 1
+    [ "$status" -eq 0 ]
+    [[ "$output" == *"WARN: Bridgebuilder review iter 1 exited 1 (the review did not complete)"* ]]
+    [[ "$output" == *"GATE_RC=0"* ]]
+}
+
+@test "spiral-harness: every entry.sh invocation goes through _bb_surface_exit (no bare || true)" {
+    local script="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/scripts/spiral-harness.sh"
+    local invocations surfaced
+    invocations=$(grep -c '"\$entry_script" --pr' "$script")
+    surfaced=$(grep -c '_bb_surface_exit "\$bb_rc"' "$script")
+    [ "$invocations" -ge 2 ]
+    [ "$invocations" -eq "$surfaced" ]
+}
+
+@test "entry.sh: the missing-dependency preflight exits 4, never the DEGRADED code 3" {
+    local entry="$PROJECT_ROOT/.claude/skills/bridgebuilder-review/resources/entry.sh"
+    run grep -n '^  exit 3$' "$entry"
+    [ "$status" -ne 0 ]
+    run grep -c '^  exit 4$' "$entry"
+    [ "$output" = "1" ]
+}
